metinler.baslik: Landing at Samsun: The General Situation
metinler.dinleyen: 2nd Grand Congress of the Republican People's Party · Ankara, 15 October 1927

satirlar.o: 1335 senesi Mayıs'ının on dokuzuncu günü Samsun'a çıktım.
satirlar.s: I landed at Samsun on 19 May 1919. (1335 is 1919 in the Rumi calendar used at the time.)

satirlar.o: Vaziyet ve manzara-i umumiye:
satirlar.s: This was the general situation and outlook:

satirlar.o: Osmanlı Devleti'nin dahil bulunduğu grup, Harb-i Umumi'de mağlup olmuş,
satirlar.s: The alliance the Ottoman State belonged to had been defeated in the First World War,

satirlar.o: Osmanlı ordusu her tarafta zedelenmiş, şeraiti ağır bir mütarekename imzalanmış.
satirlar.s: the army was worn down on every front, and a harsh armistice had been signed.

satirlar.o: Büyük Harbin uzun seneleri zarfında, millet yorgun ve fakir bir halde.
satirlar.s: After long years of war the nation was exhausted and poor.

satirlar.o: Millet ve memleketi Harb-i Umumi'ye sevk edenler, kendi hayatları endişesine düşerek memleketten firar etmişler.
satirlar.s: Those who had dragged the nation into the war had fled the country to save their own skins.

satirlar.o: Ordunun elinden esliha ve cephanesi alınmış ve alınmakta.
satirlar.s: The army had been stripped of its weapons and ammunition, and still was being stripped.

satirlar: Four days earlier, on 15 May, the Greek army had landed at İzmir. The French were at Adana, the British on the Antep–Maraş–Urfa line, the Italians at Antalya and Konya.
metinler.ne: Nutuk's famous first sentence and the state of the country in the spring of 1919.
metinler.bilgi: Nutuk's first sentence gives the date in the Rumi calendar: 1335. The Ottomans used the Rumi calendar then; Turkey moved to the international calendar on 1 January 1926. Mustafa Kemal left Istanbul on the steamer Bandırma on 16 May 1919.
metinler.vk: Nutuk/1. bölüm/Samsun'a çıktığım gün umumî vaziyet ve manzara

vk.title: Nutuk/1. bölüm/Samsun'a çıktığım gün umumî vaziyet ve manzara

metinler.baslik: There Was Only One Decision
metinler.dinleyen: 2nd Grand Congress of the Republican People's Party · Ankara, 15 October 1927
satirlar: At the time three ways of deliverance were being put forward.
The first was to ask for British protection, the second to accept an American mandate.
The third was for each region to fend for itself.
Mustafa Kemal accepted none of them: all of them gave up the nation's independence.

satirlar.o: Efendiler, bu vaziyet karşısında bir tek karar vardı.
satirlar.s: Gentlemen, in these circumstances there was only one decision.

satirlar.o: O da hâkimiyet-i milliyeye müstenid, bilâkayd ü şart müstakil yeni bir Türk Devleti tesis etmek!
satirlar.s: It was to found a new Turkish State, based on national sovereignty and unconditionally independent!

satirlar: According to Nutuk this decision was made before leaving Istanbul and put into practice the moment he set foot on Anatolian soil at Samsun.
metinler.ne: The decision for full independence against the talk of mandates and protection.
metinler.bilgi: A 'mandate' meant handing a country's government to a great power. The idea was rejected for good at the Sivas Congress.

metinler.baslik: The Amasya Circular: The Nation's Resolve Will Save Its Independence
metinler.dinleyen: Secret circular to all civil and military authorities
satirlar: After rousing the people with meetings at Havza, Mustafa Kemal met his comrades-in-arms at Amasya.

satirlar.o: Vatanın tamamiyeti, milletin istiklali tehlikededir.
satirlar.s: The integrity of the country and the independence of the nation are in danger.

satirlar.o: Hükümet-i merkeziye deruhde ettiği mes'ûliyetin icâbâtını ifa edememektedir.
satirlar.s: The Istanbul government cannot carry out the responsibility it has taken on.

satirlar.o: Milletin istiklalini yine milletin azim ve kararı kurtaracaktır.
satirlar.s: The nation's own resolve and determination will save the nation's independence.

satirlar: It was decided that a national congress representing the whole country should meet at Sivas.
The circular was signed by Mustafa Kemal with Rauf, Ali Fuat and Refet; Kâzım Karabekir joined by telegraph.
metinler.ne: The first document to state together the aim, the reason and the method of the National Struggle.
metinler.bilgi: The Amasya Circular was secret, but for the first time it declared 'the nation' master of its own fate. That is why it is called the 'declaration of revolution' of the War of Independence.
metinler.vk: Nutuk/2. bölüm/Sivas'ta umumi bir millî heyet toplama kararı

vk.title: Nutuk/2. bölüm/Sivas'ta umumi bir millî heyet toplama kararı

metinler.baslik: Resigning from the Army: As One of the Nation
metinler.dinleyen: By telegraph to Istanbul and the army corps
satirlar: The Istanbul government had dismissed Mustafa Kemal and ordered him to return at once.
On the night of 8 July 1919 he sat down at the telegraph in Erzurum.
He announced that he was resigning both his official post and the army.
He no longer had rank or office; he would carry on the struggle as one of the nation.
He gave up the profession he loved most, soldiering, for the cause.
Kâzım Karabekir, commander of the XVth Corps, did not arrest him; on the contrary, he declared himself at his orders.
metinler.ne: The decision to lay down every official title and carry on the struggle as a civilian.
metinler.bilgi: The National Struggle was largely run by telegraph. Nutuk is full of ciphered telegrams, orders and replies; Mustafa Kemal and his comrades spent many nights at the telegraph.
metinler.vk: Nutuk/2. bölüm/Resmî sıfat ve salâhiyetleri bırakarak milletin şefkat ve civanmertliğine güvenmek ve vicdani vazifeye devam etmek kararı

vk.title: Nutuk/2. bölüm/Resmî sıfat ve salâhiyetleri bırakarak milletin şefkat ve civanmertliğine güvenmek ve vicdani vazifeye devam etmek kararı

metinler.baslik: The Erzurum Congress: The Homeland Is One Whole
satirlar: On 23 July 1919 delegates of the eastern provinces met at Erzurum.
Mustafa Kemal was elected chairman of the congress.
Resolution: within the national frontiers the homeland is one whole and cannot be divided.
The nation will resist together every foreign occupation and interference.
If the Istanbul government cannot protect the homeland, a provisional government will be formed.
Mandates and protection are unacceptable.

satirlar.o: Kuvâ-yı milliyeyi âmil ve irâde-i milliyeyi hâkim kılmak esastır.
satirlar.s: The principle is to make the national forces the driving power and the national will sovereign.

satirlar: The congress closed on 7 August; Mustafa Kemal headed the Representative Committee it elected.
metinler.ne: The first congress that met regionally but decided for the whole homeland.
metinler.bilgi: The Erzurum Congress's 'national frontiers' resolution is counted as the first draft of the National Pact.
metinler.vk: Nutuk/2. bölüm/Erzurum Kongresi beyannamesi ve kararları

vk.title: Nutuk/2. bölüm/Erzurum Kongresi beyannamesi ve kararları

metinler.baslik: The Sivas Congress: All Societies Under One Roof
satirlar: On 4 September 1919 delegates from every part of Anatolia and Rumelia met at Sivas.
All the national societies were united under the name 'Society for the Defence of the Rights of Anatolia and Rumelia'.
The principle laid down at Erzurum was repeated here for the whole country: the national forces would be the driving power and the national will sovereign.
The idea of a mandate or protection was rejected for good.
The Istanbul government's attempts to break up the congress came to nothing; Anatolia cut its telegraph links with Istanbul.
At the beginning of October the Damat Ferit government fell. Anatolia now spoke with one voice.
metinler.ne: Here the organisation of the National Struggle covering the whole country was founded.
metinler.bilgi: During the congress Mustafa Kemal and his comrades stayed at the telegraph until morning. The telegraph lines were like the 'live broadcast' of those days.

metinler.baslik: Arrival in Ankara: The Heart of the Struggle
metinler.dinleyen: 2nd Grand Congress of the Republican People's Party · Ankara, 1927
satirlar: The Representative Committee arrived in Ankara on 27 December 1919.
Ankara was on the railway, close enough to Istanbul and far enough from the front.
The people, the seymen and the efe welcomed the Committee with joy.
A small Anatolian town would become the capital of the new state within a few years.
metinler.ne: The Representative Committee's choice of Ankara as its centre.
metinler.bilgi: Ankara was officially declared the capital on 13 October 1923, two weeks before the proclamation of the Republic.

metinler.baslik: The National Pact and the Occupation of Istanbul
metinler.dinleyen: 2nd Grand Congress of the Republican People's Party · Ankara, 1927
satirlar: The last Ottoman Chamber of Deputies adopted the National Pact on 28 January 1920.
Under it, the lands held when the armistice was signed and inhabited mostly by Turks were one indivisible whole.
The Allies answered by formally occupying Istanbul on 16 March 1920.
The Chamber was raided; some deputies were arrested and exiled to Malta.
Mustafa Kemal acted the same day: an assembly with extraordinary powers would meet in Ankara.
metinler.ne: The declaration of the national frontiers and Ankara's answer to the occupation of Istanbul.
metinler.bilgi: The National Pact was the compass of Turkish diplomacy all the way to Lausanne.

metinler.baslik: 23 April 1920: The Grand National Assembly Opens
satirlar: On Friday 23 April 1920 the Grand National Assembly of Turkey opened in Ankara.
In the nation's name the Assembly took both legislative and executive power into its own hands.
Mustafa Kemal was elected President of the Assembly.
The first article of the first constitution, adopted in January 1921, wrote down the principle:

satirlar.o: Hâkimiyet bilâkaydüşart milletindir.
satirlar.s: Sovereignty belongs to the nation without condition.

metinler.ne: The birth of a new assembly founded on national sovereignty.
metinler.bilgi: Today 'Sovereignty belongs unconditionally to the nation' is written in the Grand National Assembly's main hall.
metinler.vk: Nutuk/10. bölüm/Teşkilât-ı Esasiye Kanununun esas maddelerini Tevfik Paşa'ya bildirdim

vk.title: Nutuk/10. bölüm/Teşkilât-ı Esasiye Kanununun esas maddelerini Tevfik Paşa'ya bildirdim

metinler.baslik: İnönü: You Have Also Defeated the Nation's Ill Fate
metinler.dinleyen: İsmet Pasha, commander of the Western Front
satirlar: The regular army passed its first test on the Western Front, at İnönü, under İsmet Pasha.
The First Battle of İnönü in January 1921 raised the Assembly's standing.
At the end of March the Greek army attacked again; the Second Battle of İnönü was won on 31 March 1921.
Mustafa Kemal watched the battlefield from Metristepe and sent İsmet Pasha this telegram:

satirlar.o: Siz orada yalnız düşmanı değil, milletin makûs talihini de yendiniz.
satirlar.s: There you have defeated not only the enemy but also the nation's ill fate.

metinler.ne: The regular army's first victories and a telegram that went down in history.
metinler.bilgi: İsmet Pasha took the surname 'İnönü' under the 1934 Surname Law; it comes from these victories.
metinler.vk: Nutuk/11. bölüm/İkinci İnönü Zaferi ve İsmet Paşa'nın Metristepe'de gördüğü vaziyet

vk.title: Nutuk/11. bölüm/İkinci İnönü Zaferi ve İsmet Paşa'nın Metristepe'de gördüğü vaziyet

metinler.baslik: Sakarya: There Is No Line of Defence, There Is a Plain of Defence
satirlar: After the defeat at Kütahya–Eskişehir the army fell back east of the Sakarya River.
On 5 August 1921 the Assembly gave Mustafa Kemal the powers of Commander-in-Chief for three months.
Under the National Requisition orders the people gave part of what they had to the army: socks, sandals, wheat, horses, ox-carts.

satirlar.o: Hatt-ı müdafaa yoktur, sath-ı müdafaa vardır. O satıh bütün vatandır.
satirlar.s: There is no line to defend, there is a plain to defend. That plain is the whole homeland.

satirlar.o: Vatanın her karış toprağı, vatandaşın kanıyla ıslanmadıkça terk olunamaz.
satirlar.s: Not an inch of the homeland may be given up until it is soaked in the blood of its citizens.

satirlar: The battle lasted 22 days and 22 nights and ended in victory on 13 September 1921.
The Assembly gave Mustafa Kemal the rank of Marshal and the title of Gazi.
metinler.ne: The turning point of the war and the order to defend the 'plain'.
metinler.bilgi: After Sakarya the Greek army never attacked again. The Treaty of Ankara with France (20 October 1921) was signed right after this victory.
metinler.vk: Nutuk/12. bölüm/Hatt-ı müdafaa yoktur, sath-ı müdafaa vardır

vk.title: Nutuk/12. bölüm/Hatt-ı müdafaa yoktur, sath-ı müdafaa vardır

metinler.baslik: Armies! Your First Goal Is the Mediterranean
satirlar: On the morning of 26 August 1922 the Great Offensive began from Kocatepe.
On 30 August the Commander-in-Chief's Battle was won at Dumlupınar.
On 1 September the Commander-in-Chief gave the army this order:

satirlar.o: Ordular! İlk hedefiniz Akdeniz'dir. İleri!

satirlar: On 9 September 1922 Turkish cavalry entered İzmir.
On 11 October the Armistice of Mudanya was signed; Eastern Thrace was recovered without a fight.
metinler.ne: The last and decisive victory of the War of Independence.
metinler.bilgi: 30 August is celebrated every year as Victory Day. Fahrettin Pasha's cavalry were among the first units to enter İzmir.
metinler.vk: Nutuk/13. bölüm/Ordularımız İzmir rıhtımında ilk verdiğim hedefe, Akdeniz'e vâsıl oldular

vk.title: Nutuk/13. bölüm/Ordularımız İzmir rıhtımında ilk verdiğim hedefe, Akdeniz'e vâsıl oldular

metinler.baslik: Sovereignty and Sultanate: 1 November 1922
satirlar: The invitation of both Ankara and Istanbul to the peace talks showed it was time to end the double rule.
When the debate in the Assembly committee dragged on, Mustafa Kemal took the floor:

satirlar.o: Hâkimiyet ve saltanat hiç kimse tarafından hiç kimseye, ilim icabıdır diye, müzakere ile, münakaşa ile verilmez.
satirlar.s: Sovereignty and sultanate are not given to anyone by debate and discussion because scholarship requires it.

satirlar.o: Hâkimiyet, saltanat, kuvvetle, kudretle ve zorla alınır.
satirlar.s: Sovereignty and sultanate are taken by strength, by power and by force.

satirlar: The sultanate was abolished on 1 November 1922.
The last sultan, Vahdettin, left the country on a British warship on 17 November.
metinler.ne: The end of a six-century sultanate.
metinler.bilgi: So the Ottoman sultanate, which had lasted 623 years from 1299 to 1922, formally came to an end.

metinler.baslik: Lausanne: The New Turkey at the Table
metinler.dinleyen: 2nd Grand Congress of the Republican People's Party · Ankara, 1927
satirlar: The delegation led by İsmet Pasha negotiated at Lausanne for months.
The talks broke down in February 1923 and resumed in April.
The treaty signed on 24 July 1923 introduced the new Turkish state to the world.
The centuries-old capitulations were abolished.
Some questions, such as Mosul and the Straits, were left for later; the Straits came under full Turkish control with the Montreux Convention of 1936.
metinler.ne: The War of Independence's victory at the table.
metinler.bilgi: At the head of the Turkish delegation at Lausanne was a soldier, İsmet Pasha. He was hard of hearing, and it is said that at difficult moments he 'chose not to hear'.

metinler.baslik: Tomorrow We Shall Proclaim the Republic!
metinler.dinleyen: His friends at dinner at Çankaya
satirlar: In October 1923 there was a government crisis; no cabinet could be formed.
At dinner at Çankaya on the evening of 28 October, Mustafa Kemal told his friends:

satirlar.o: Yarın Cumhuriyet ilân edeceğiz!
satirlar.s: Tomorrow we shall proclaim the Republic!

satirlar: On the evening of 29 October 1923 the Assembly amended the constitution and proclaimed the Republic.
That same night Mustafa Kemal was unanimously elected the first President; İsmet Pasha became Prime Minister.
A 101-gun salute was fired in Ankara.
metinler.ne: The night the Republic was proclaimed.
metinler.bilgi: On the evening of 29 October 1923 Mustafa Kemal was elected the first President by the unanimous vote of the 158 deputies present.

wiki.en: Proclamation of the Republic of Turkey

metinler.vk: Nutuk/16. bölüm/Cumhuriyetin ilânı kararını nerede ve kimlere söyledim

vk.title: Nutuk/16. bölüm/Cumhuriyetin ilânı kararını nerede ve kimlere söyledim

metinler.baslik: 3 March 1924: Education Under One Roof
satirlar: On 3 March 1924 the Assembly passed three important laws on the same day.
The Caliphate was abolished; the Ottoman dynasty was sent abroad.
With the Law on the Unification of Education, all schools were brought under one roof, the Ministry of Education.
The Ministry of Religious Law and Foundations was abolished; the Presidency of Religious Affairs was set up in its place.
On 20 April of the same year the new constitution was adopted.
metinler.ne: A great step towards a unified education and a secular state.
metinler.bilgi: Tevhid-i Tedrisat means 'unification of education': medreses, schools and foreign schools were joined in one education system.
metinler.vk: Nutuk/17. bölüm/Hilâfetin, Şer'iye ve Evkaf Vekâletlerinin lağvı ve tedrisatın tevhîdi kararı

vk.title: Nutuk/17. bölüm/Hilâfetin, Şer'iye ve Evkaf Vekâletlerinin lağvı ve tedrisatın tevhîdi kararı

metinler.baslik: Six Days, Thirty-Six and a Half Hours: Nutuk Is Read
metinler.dinleyen: 2nd Grand Congress of the Republican People's Party
satirlar: On 15 October 1927 the Second Grand Congress of the Republican People's Party met in Ankara.
The Gazi took the rostrum and spoke for six days, close to thirty-six and a half hours in all.
He told everything that happened from 1919 to 1927 one by one, with documents, telegrams and orders.
Most of his listeners had witnessed the events; the speech was prepared like an accounting.
On 20 October 1927 he spoke his last words to the Turkish youth.
Nutuk was printed the same year in Arabic letters, together with a volume of documents.
metinler.ne: The story of Nutuk itself.
metinler.bilgi: The Gazi wrote Nutuk after months of preparation, choosing the documents one by one. That is why its volume of documents holds hundreds of telegrams, orders and letters.

metinler.baslik: Address to the Youth

satirlar.o: Ey Türk gençliği! Birinci vazifen, Türk istiklalini, Türk Cumhuriyetini, ilelebet muhafaza ve müdafaa etmektir.
satirlar.s: O Turkish Youth! Your first duty is to preserve and defend Turkish independence and the Turkish Republic for ever.

satirlar.o: Mevcudiyetinin ve istikbalinin yegâne temeli budur. Bu temel, senin en kıymetli hazinendir.
satirlar.s: This is the only basis of your existence and your future. This basis is your most precious treasure.

satirlar.o: İstikbalde dahi, seni bu hazineden mahrum etmek isteyecek dahilî ve haricî bedhahların olacaktır.
satirlar.s: In the future, too, there will be ill-wishers at home and abroad who want to deprive you of this treasure.

satirlar.o: Bir gün, istiklal ve cumhuriyeti müdafaa mecburiyetine düşersen, vazifeye atılmak için, içinde bulunacağın vaziyetin imkân ve şeraitini düşünmeyeceksin!
satirlar.s: If one day you are compelled to defend your independence and the Republic, you will not stop to weigh the possibilities and conditions of the situation you are in before taking up your duty!

satirlar.o: Bu imkân ve şerait, çok namüsait bir mahiyette tezahür edebilir.
satirlar.s: These possibilities and conditions may be extremely unfavourable.

satirlar.o: İstiklal ve cumhuriyetine kastedecek düşmanlar, bütün dünyada emsali görülmemiş bir galibiyetin mümessili olabilirler.
satirlar.s: The enemies plotting against your independence and your Republic may be the representatives of a victory unseen in the world.

satirlar.o: Cebren ve hile ile aziz vatanın bütün kaleleri zapt edilmiş, bütün tersanelerine girilmiş, bütün orduları dağıtılmış ve memleketin her köşesi bilfiil işgal edilmiş olabilir.
satirlar.s: By force and by trickery, all the fortresses of your beloved homeland may have been captured, all its shipyards entered, all its armies dispersed and every corner of the country actually occupied.

satirlar.o: Bütün bu şeraitten daha elîm ve daha vahim olmak üzere, memleketin dahilinde iktidara sahip olanlar gaflet ve dalalet ve hatta hıyanet içinde bulunabilirler.
satirlar.s: More bitter and more dangerous than all this, those who hold power within the country may be in error, misguided, even traitors.

satirlar.o: Hatta bu iktidar sahipleri şahsi menfaatlerini, müstevlilerin siyasi emelleriyle tevhid edebilirler.
satirlar.s: These rulers may even join their personal interests to the political aims of the invaders.

satirlar.o: Millet, fakr u zaruret içinde harap ve bitap düşmüş olabilir.
satirlar.s: The nation may be ruined and exhausted by poverty and hardship.

satirlar.o: Ey Türk istikbalinin evladı! İşte, bu ahval ve şerait içinde dahi vazifen, Türk istiklal ve cumhuriyetini kurtarmaktır!
satirlar.s: O child of Turkey's future! Even in these circumstances and conditions, your duty is to save Turkish independence and the Republic!

satirlar.o: Muhtaç olduğun kudret, damarlarındaki asil kanda mevcuttur!
satirlar.s: The strength you need is in the noble blood in your veins!

metinler.ne: The last words of Nutuk: the Republic entrusted to the youth.
metinler.bilgi: The Address to the Youth was delivered on 20 October 1927, the last day of the reading of Nutuk. Today it hangs on the wall of most schools in Turkey.

metinler.baslik: Arıburnu: I Do Not Order You to Attack
satirlar: On the morning of 25 April 1915 the Allied forces landed at Arıburnu.
Lieutenant Colonel Mustafa Kemal, commander of the 19th Division, sent his units to Conkbayırı without waiting for orders.
The order he gave the 57th Regiment went down in history:

satirlar.o: Ben size taarruzu emretmiyorum, ölmeyi emrediyorum.
satirlar.s: I do not order you to attack; I order you to die.

satirlar.o: Biz ölünceye kadar geçecek zaman zarfında yerimize başka kuvvetler ve kumandanlar kaim olabilir.
satirlar.s: In the time it takes us to die, other troops and commanders can come and take our places.

satirlar: Most of the soldiers of the 57th Regiment fell that day.
Today there is no regiment numbered 57 in the Turkish army: the number is kept in their memory.
metinler.ne: The day at Gallipoli that brought Mustafa Kemal onto the stage of history.
metinler.bilgi: After the battles of Anafartalar and Conkbayırı in August 1915, Mustafa Kemal became known as the 'Hero of Anafartalar'.

metinler.baslik: The İzmir Economic Congress: Military Victory Is Not Enough
metinler.dinleyen: Representatives of farmers, merchants, industrialists and workers
satirlar: The Lausanne talks had broken off; the Gazi called a congress in İzmir to draw the road map of the economy.
Representatives of farmers, merchants, industrialists and workers met in the same hall for the first time.

satirlar.o: Siyasi, askerî zaferler ne kadar büyük olursa olsunlar, iktisadi zaferlerle tetviç edilmezlerse husule gelen zaferler payidar olamaz, az zamanda söner.
satirlar.s: However great political and military victories may be, unless they are crowned by economic victories they cannot last and soon fade.

satirlar: The congress took decisions to support local production: the 'Economic Pact' was adopted.
metinler.ne: The idea that independence must be completed by the economy.
metinler.bilgi: About 1,100 delegates attended; Kâzım Karabekir chaired the congress.

metinler.baslik: The Truest Guide Is Science
satirlar: In September 1924, on his Black Sea tour, the Gazi spoke to teachers at Samsun.

satirlar.o: Dünyada her şey için, medeniyet için, hayat için, muvaffakiyet için en hakiki mürşit ilimdir, fendir.
satirlar.s: For everything in the world, for civilisation, for life, for success, the truest guide is science and technique.

satirlar.o: İlim ve fennin haricinde mürşit aramak gaflettir, cehalettir, dalalettir.
satirlar.s: To look for a guide outside science and technique is heedlessness, ignorance, straying from the right path.

satirlar.o: Yalnız, ilmin ve fennin yaşadığımız her dakikadaki safhalarının tekâmülünü idrak etmek ve terakkiyatını zamanında takip eylemek şarttır.
satirlar.s: But it is essential to grasp the ever-changing growth of science and technique and to follow its advances in time.

satirlar.o: Bin, iki bin, binlerce sene evvelki ilim ve fen lisanının çizdiği düsturları, şu kadar bin sene sonra bugün aynen tatbik etmeye kalkışmak, elbette ilim ve fennin içinde bulunmak değildir.
satirlar.s: Trying to apply today, unchanged, the rules laid down by the science of thousands of years ago is certainly not being within science.

metinler.ne: A call to take science as the guide.
metinler.bilgi: The short form of these words, 'The truest guide in life is science', is written on the front of Ankara University's Faculty of Language, History and Geography.

metinler.baslik: Sarayburnu: The New Turkish Letters
satirlar: On the night of 9 August 1928 the Gazi took the rostrum at a festival in Gülhane Park.

satirlar.o: Bizim ahenktar, zengin lisanımız yeni Türk harfleriyle kendini gösterecektir.
satirlar.s: Our harmonious, rich language will show itself with the new Turkish letters.

satirlar: He asked the people to learn the new letters quickly and to teach them to every woman and man, to porters and boatmen.
He told them to see this as a patriotic duty.
He stressed that it was shameful so few people could read and write.
Then the Gazi stood at the blackboard and began teaching the new letters himself.
The Alphabet Law was passed on 1 November 1928; the Nation's Schools opened on 1 January 1929.
metinler.ne: The night the Alphabet Reform was first explained to the people.
metinler.bilgi: The Gazi taught the new letters at the blackboard in many cities; that is why he is remembered as the 'Head Teacher'.

metinler.baslik: The Tenth Anniversary Speech
metinler.dinleyen: To the whole nation · on the radio

satirlar.o: Türk Milleti! Kurtuluş savaşına başladığımızın on beşinci yılı içindeyiz.
satirlar.s: Turkish Nation! We are in the fifteenth year since we began the War of Independence.

satirlar.o: Bugün Cumhuriyetimizin onuncu yılını doldurduğu en büyük bayramdır. Kutlu olsun.
satirlar.s: Today is the greatest festival, the completion of our Republic's tenth year. May it be blessed.

satirlar.o: Yurttaşlarım! Az zamanda çok ve büyük işler yaptık.
satirlar.s: My fellow citizens! In a short time we have done many great things.

satirlar.o: Bu işlerin en büyüğü, temeli Türk kahramanlığı ve yüksek Türk kültürü olan Türkiye Cumhuriyetidir.
satirlar.s: The greatest of them is the Republic of Turkey, founded on Turkish heroism and lofty Turkish culture.

satirlar.o: Fakat yaptıklarımızı asla kâfi göremeyiz. Çünkü daha çok ve daha büyüklerini yapmak mecburiyetinde ve azmindeyiz.
satirlar.s: But we can never think what we have done enough, because we must do still more and greater things, and we are determined to.

satirlar.o: Yurdumuzu dünyanın en mamur ve en medeni memleketleri seviyesine çıkaracağız.
satirlar.s: We shall raise our country to the level of the most prosperous and civilised countries in the world.

satirlar.o: Milletimizi en geniş refah vasıta ve kaynaklarına sahip kılacağız.
satirlar.s: We shall give our nation the widest means and sources of prosperity.

satirlar.o: Millî kültürümüzü muasır medeniyet seviyesinin üstüne çıkaracağız.
satirlar.s: We shall raise our national culture above the level of contemporary civilisation.

satirlar.o: Bunun için, bizce zaman ölçüsü, geçmiş asırların gevşetici zihniyetine göre değil, asrımızın sürat ve hareket mefhumuna göre düşünülmelidir.
satirlar.s: For this, our measure of time must follow not the slack mind of past centuries but the speed and movement of our age.

satirlar.o: Ne mutlu Türküm diyene!

metinler.ne: Speech to the nation in the Republic's 10th year.
metinler.bilgi: The Tenth Anniversary Speech was broadcast on the radio and filmed; it is one of the best-known surviving recordings of Atatürk's voice and image.

metinler.baslik: Civic Knowledge: The Republic Is Virtue
satirlar: In 1930 the Gazi dictated his notes on citizenship to Afet Hanım.
These notes were taught in schools as a textbook called 'Civic Knowledge'.
The book explained the nation, the state, sovereignty, elections, taxes and freedom in plain language.
What the Republic expected of its citizen was a person who thinks and takes responsibility.
The book's most quoted idea is: the Republic is a government founded on high moral virtue.
metinler.ne: Atatürk's notes on citizenship.
metinler.bilgi: The handwritten pages of these notes were later published as 'Civic Knowledge and the Handwriting of M. Kemal Atatürk'.

metinler.baslik: Geometry: Angle, Triangle, Radius
satirlar: In the winter of 1936–37 Atatürk wrote a short book for geometry lessons.
The aim was to replace terms of Arabic and Persian origin with Turkish words.
Zaviye became 'açı' (angle), müselles 'üçgen' (triangle), kutur 'çap' (diameter), nısf-ı kutur 'yarıçap' (radius).
Ufki became 'yatay' (horizontal), amudi 'dikey' (vertical), mümas 'teğet' (tangent), müsavi 'eşit' (equal).
The book was published by the Ministry of Culture in 1937 without the author's name.
Most of these words every pupil uses today spread through that little book.
metinler.ne: Mathematical terms Atatürk gave to Turkish.
metinler.bilgi: The geometry book was printed without its author's name; it was revealed later to be Atatürk's work. Words such as 'toplam, artı, eksi, çarpı, bölü' (sum, plus, minus, times, divided by) also took root in this period.

metinler.baslik: The Will: His Fortune to History and Language
satirlar: Atatürk wrote his will in his own hand at Dolmabahçe Palace on 5 September 1938.
He left all his cash and movable property to the Republican People's Party.
From the income of his İş Bankası shares he asked for monthly allowances to his sister Makbule and his adopted children.
He also wrote that İsmet İnönü's children should be helped with their higher education from this income.
He willed that the remaining income be shared equally between the Turkish Historical Society and the Turkish Language Association.
metinler.ne: A founder of a state leaving his fortune to science and language.
metinler.bilgi: The Turkish Historical Society was founded in 1931 and the Turkish Language Association in 1932 under Atatürk's leadership. The will was meant to support them after his death.

metinler.baslik: 10 November 1938, 9:05
satirlar: On the morning of Thursday 10 November 1938, at five past nine, Atatürk closed his eyes at Dolmabahçe Palace.
He was 57.
His coffin passed before the people in Istanbul and was then taken to Ankara.
On 21 November 1938 he was laid in a temporary tomb at the Ethnography Museum.
On 10 November 1953 he was moved to Anıtkabir.
Every year on 10 November at 9:05 the sirens sound and Turkey stops for a moment.
metinler.ne: The day he walked into immortality.
metinler.bilgi: It is said the clocks in his room at Dolmabahçe were stopped at 9:05; the room is open to visitors today.

biliyormu: 🎙️ Nutuk was read over 6 days, 15–20 October 1927, in about 36.5 hours
🚢 The steamer Bandırma left Istanbul for Samsun on 16 May 1919
📐 The book 'Geometry' was printed in 1937 without an author's name; its author was Atatürk
✍️ The surname 'Atatürk' was given on 24 November 1934 by a special law of the Assembly
⏳ The Battle of the Sakarya lasted 22 days and 22 nights
🎼 Mehmet Akif refused the prize money of the Independence March competition
🗳️ On the night the Republic was proclaimed, 158 deputies elected Mustafa Kemal unanimously
🔤 Adults learned the new letters in the Nation's Schools, opened on 1 January 1929
🎖️ There is no regiment numbered 57 in the Turkish army: in memory of Gallipoli
🏛️ Ankara became the capital on 13 October 1923, two weeks before the Republic
👩 Women won the vote in municipal elections in 1930, village elections in 1933 and parliamentary elections in 1934
🕰️ The international clock and calendar came into use on 1 January 1926
📏 The Measures Law of 1931 brought in the metre and the kilogram
📅 The weekly holiday moved from Friday to Sunday in 1935
👋 In 1934 titles such as 'efendi, bey, pasha' were abolished; 'Bay' and 'Bayan' (Mr and Mrs) took their place
🔬 'The truest guide in life is science' is written on the front of the Faculty of Language, History and Geography in Ankara
📡 The National Struggle was largely run by telegraph; Nutuk is full of telegrams
📚 By Atatürk's will, the income of his İş Bankası shares went to the Turkish Historical and Language societies

dogrumu.soz: The future is in the skies.
dogrumu.nerede: Posters, aviation ceremonies, a speech made from space in 2024
dogrumu.kanit: No date, place or record has ever been shown for this much-loved saying. Arı İnan, Afet İnan's daughter, said she searched for a long time but found no record of it; Sabiha Gökçen could not recall it either.
dogrumu.tarihci: The importance Atatürk gave to aviation is documented; that this sentence is his is not.
dogrumu.kisaca: The idea is his; the sentence has no source.

dogrumu.soz: Peace at home, peace in the world.
dogrumu.nerede: The preamble of the Constitution, school books
dogrumu.kanit: It appears in the election manifesto published over the signature 'Gazi Mustafa Kemal' on 20 April 1931: 'We work for peace at home and peace in the world.'
dogrumu.tarihci: The sentence later entered the preambles of the 1961 and 1982 constitutions.

dogrumu.soz: There is no difference between the Johnnies and the Mehmets to us…
dogrumu.nerede: The Anzac Cove memorial at Gallipoli and memorials in Australia and New Zealand
dogrumu.kanit: The text is traced to an address to the Anzacs by Interior Minister Şükrü Kaya in 1934. No record from Atatürk's own mouth or pen has been shown; some researchers argue that today's form of the text appeared in the 1950s.
dogrumu.tarihci: Its spirit fits Atatürk's policy of peace, but the documents are not enough to call it 'his words'.
dogrumu.kisaca: Indirect source; the debate goes on.

dogrumu.soz: How happy is the one who says I am a Turk!
dogrumu.kanit: It is the last sentence of the Tenth Anniversary Speech read in Ankara on 29 October 1933; the speech was broadcast on the radio and filmed.
dogrumu.tarihci: The sound and film recording of the speech survives.

dogrumu.soz: There is no line of defence, there is a plain of defence. That plain is the whole homeland.
dogrumu.kanit: The idea given to the army in the Battle of the Sakarya; the Gazi quotes it himself in Nutuk.
dogrumu.tarihci: It is in Nutuk; it sums up the defence at Sakarya.

dogrumu.soz: The truest guide in life is science.
dogrumu.nerede: The front of Ankara University's Faculty of Language, History and Geography, school notice boards
dogrumu.kanit: It comes from his talk to teachers at Samsun in September 1924: 'For everything in the world, for civilisation, for life, for success, the truest guide is science and technique.'
dogrumu.tarihci: The common short form sums up the original sentence; the meaning is the same.
dogrumu.kisaca: Documented; the short form is a summary.

dogrumu.soz: Nutuk was read in a single day, in one breath.
dogrumu.kanit: Nutuk was read on six separate days, 15–20 October 1927; it lasted more than 36 hours in all.
dogrumu.tarihci: Not one day but six. Still, it is one of the longest speeches ever given by a single speaker.
dogrumu.kisaca: Wrong: it was read over six days.

dogrumu.kanit: The book 'Geometry', printed in 1937 without an author's name, is Atatürk's; it uses Turkish terms such as açı (angle) instead of zaviye and üçgen (triangle) instead of müselles.
dogrumu.tarihci: It was later revealed that Atatürk wrote the book; he coined some of the terms himself.
